_why:
Four edges resting on two Intercept pieces, both opened and read: Keith Kloor, 'The Media Loves This UFO Expert Who Says He Worked for an Obscure Pentagon Program. Did He?', 1 June 2019, and Ken Klippenstein, 'UFO Whistleblower Kept Security Clearance After Psychiatric Detention', 9 August 2023.

The Kloor piece carries three of the four on its own, and it is worth noting why one document sources three different edges honestly rather than by shared-URL autofill: each of the three relationships is separately asserted IN the piece. It names the Pentagon spokesperson who confirmed AATIP existed (Christopher Sherwood), it reports TTSA's own SEC filing describing the company as a 'Motion Picture & Video Tape Production' concern, and it states the finding about Elizondo. Three assertions, three edges.

The Hill's three edges are left unsourced. thehill.com returns 403 to this environment on every URL tried, including ones already cited on the board from an earlier pass. They cannot be opened here and so are not cited here.

sources.name: Keith Kloor, 'The Media Loves This UFO Expert Who Says He Worked for an Obscure Pentagon Program. Did He?', The Intercept, 1 June 2019

edges.note: Kloor's finding: 'There is no discernible evidence that Luis Elizondo ever worked for a government UFO program, much less led one.' He obtained a statement from Pentagon spokesperson Christopher Sherwood: 'Mr. Elizondo had no responsibilities with regard to the AATIP program while he worked in OUSDI... up until the time he resigned effective 10/4/2017.' The piece is the origin of the documented dispute over Elizondo's role, and the Pentagon's position in it has been restated since.

In the same piece the Pentagon confirmed to The Intercept, through spokesperson Christopher Sherwood, that AATIP existed and 'did pursue research and investigation into unidentified aerial phenomena', while declining to confirm the leadership claim being made for Elizondo. The programme's existence and one man's role in it were separated by the same statement.

The piece documents what To The Stars Academy's own regulatory filings say it is: a 'Motion Picture & Video Tape Production' concern. It also reports the undisclosed relationship between the company and the programme promoting it - TTSA co-founder Tom DeLonge was executive producer of the History Channel's 'Unidentified', which featured Elizondo and fellow TTSA employee Chris Mellon without the ties being disclosed on screen.

sources.name: Ken Klippenstein, 'UFO Whistleblower Kept Security Clearance After Psychiatric Detention', The Intercept, 9 August 2023

edges.note: Klippenstein obtained Loudoun County Sheriff's Office incident reports under the Virginia Freedom of Information Act showing Grusch was detained under an emergency custody order on 1 October 2018 and transferred to Loudoun Adult Medical Psychiatric Services. The piece is explicit about provenance: 'The records were not confidential, medical, or leaked. They are publicly available law enforcement records obtained under a routine Virginia FOIA request to the Loudoun County Sheriff's Office.' Its argument is about the clearance process rather than about the witness - that clearances of the kind Grusch held carry strict requirements regarding psychological episodes and substance issues, and his was retained.
